data.one_liner: Receive shared photos, videos, text, and files from other apps.
data.what_it_does: Allows your Flutter application to act as a share target, receiving content like images, videos, text, URLs, and files shared from other apps. It provides methods to handle initial sharing when the app opens and listens to a stream for incoming shares while the app is running.
use_when: Your app needs to accept shared media or text from external applications via the OS share sheet.
You want to process incoming URLs, photos, or documents sent from another app.
avoid_when: You only need to pick files from within your own app (use file_picker instead).
You do not want to configure native Android intent filters and iOS Share Extensions.
strengths: Supports multiple types of media including images, videos, text, and files.
Provides both stream subscriptions for active app states and initial sharing retrieval.
weaknesses: Requires manual and intricate native setup for both Android Manifest and iOS Share Extension.
iOS implementation requires setting up an App Group and an extension target.
data.setup_notes: Requires adding intent filters in AndroidManifest.xml and creating a Share Extension target with an App Group and custom Swift view controller on iOS.
